Introduction
I love a good image.
I love the numbers behind it.

The most dangerous assumption in marketing is that creativity and analytics live in separate departments. They do not - or at least, they shouldn't.

The best content I've made started with a question the data was asking: Why aren't students engaging with this? What does this audience actually want to see? What does the performance tell us about what to do next?

At Eagle Dining Services, Georgia Southern University, I was the person behind the Instagram - coming up with the concepts, designing the graphics, figuring out what would actually make a student stop scrolling at 11pm. At Fozzy, a grocery retail chain in Ukraine, I made the weekly promo ads - the kind of work where every price has to be right, every badge has to be readable, and there is no room for a bad week.

Across both roles, one thing stays constant: understand the audience before you pick up a design tool. And when the campaign ends, read the numbers honestly.

"I use data to find the right question - then I use creativity to answer it in a way people actually want to see."

Portfolio
The Work
01 - Eagle Dining Services
Dorm Room Cooking Made Easy
Instagram Recipe Series  ·  Utility Content
+
Target Audience
Dorm-living GSU students, primarily first and second-year, limited kitchen access
Platform
Instagram - Feed Carousels + individual recipe posts
Goal
Drive saves with genuinely useful, actionable dorm-friendly recipes
Strategic Rationale

The core insight: students already take food from the dining hall back to their rooms, but most do not know what to do with it beyond reheating. By framing recipes around ingredients students could realistically grab - tortillas, a sweet potato, ramen, grilled chicken - the content felt immediately applicable rather than aspirational. The warmer gold and navy palette felt inviting and food-forward, and the illustrated graphics kept the tone playful and accessible. Each slide was designed to be saved and referenced later. Saves were the primary metric I was optimizing for.

Results & Learnings

Saves are the highest-signal engagement action for utility content - they indicate intent to return. This series was structured so each recipe stands alone, maximizing saves, while the series format rewards followers. The "Tag us with your creation" CTA was designed to generate user content, extending organic reach beyond Eagle Dining's existing audience.

02 - Eagle Dining Services
Fueling Your Goals: Bulking vs. Cutting
Instagram Educational Carousel  ·  6-Slide Series
+
Target Audience
GSU students with fitness goals who eat at the dining hall regularly
Platform
Instagram - Multi-slide Carousel, 6 slides
Goal
Position Eagle Dining as a genuine resource for fitness-oriented students
Strategic Rationale

Fitness content consistently outperforms general nutrition content with the 18-24 demographic because it connects eating to a personal identity goal rather than abstract health guidelines. The carousel used a clean navy and cream palette with high-quality food photography, deliberately avoiding the cluttered infographic look that performs poorly on mobile. Structure was intentional: high-impact hook slide, paired deep-dives for bulking and cutting, closing with an engagement CTA. Designed to maximize both save-rate and comment engagement - the two signals that matter most for Instagram algorithmic reach.

Results & Learnings

The carousel format generates higher average time-on-post than static images, which Instagram rewards with wider distribution. Pairing educational content with a direct ask ("ask us anything") creates a natural entry point for DMs and comments, building community and giving the account ongoing response opportunities that extend organic reach.

03 - Eagle Dining Services
Leftovers, But Make It New
Instagram Campaign  ·  Food Waste Awareness Series
+
Target Audience
GSU undergrads 18-24, budget-conscious, on-campus, active on Instagram
Platform
Instagram - Feed Carousels + Static Posts
Goal
Reduce dining hall food waste through inspiration, not guilt
Strategic Rationale

Food waste messaging typically fails with college students because it leads with obligation: do not waste food. This campaign flipped that framing entirely. Instead of telling students what not to do, it showed them something aspirational - that dining hall leftovers can become genuinely good meals with almost no effort. The retro collage aesthetic with typewriter fonts, cut-paper textures, and hand-drawn gold accents felt distinct from Eagle Dining's typical institutional content and matched the visual language students were already engaging with. The series opened with a challenge hook ("Can you make something new from leftovers?") before delivering practical value.

Results & Learnings

Challenge-framing ("Can you?") outperforms instructional framing ("You should") for this demographic - it invites participation rather than compliance. Series content that opens with a question and closes with a CTA performs better than standalone posts for both reach and saves. The differentiated retro visual style was intentional to increase stop-and-read behavior in a feed dominated by standard university content.

04 - Eagle Dining Services
Video Content Series
Short-Form Video  ·  Instagram Reels
+
Target Audience
GSU students 18-24 - highest video consumption demographic on Instagram
Platform
Instagram Reels
Goal
Build authentic connection with students through human, personality-led video content
Strategic Rationale

Static graphics build awareness - video builds trust. This series was created to give Eagle Dining a human face and a personality that felt genuinely student-adjacent rather than institutional. Where the static campaigns were strategically polished, these videos leaned into spontaneity, humor, and real campus life. The goal was to attract new followers through Reels' discovery algorithm while giving existing followers a reason to actually care about the account, not just follow it.

Results & Learnings

Video content gave the account a voice that static graphics alone could not. Reels consistently reach non-followers through Instagram's Explore and Reels tab, making them the primary growth driver for the account. My personal style - low-production, high-personality - performed better with this audience than polished branded video because it felt like content students would make themselves.

05 - Fozzy Grocery Chain
Weekly Promotional Ads
E-Commerce Promotional Content  ·  Ukraine
+
Target Audience
Grocery shoppers 25-55, price-sensitive, browsing weekly deals online and in-store
Platform
Digital - website banners, e-commerce pages, social media
Goal
Drive in-store and online conversion through clear, fast-reading promotional creative
Strategic Rationale

Promotional retail content lives or dies on clarity and speed. A shopper scanning a weekly deal graphic makes a decision in under two seconds - so every design choice serves legibility first. Working within Fozzy's brand system (red, navy, white, yellow discount badges), I created ads where the price hierarchy was immediately obvious: sale price dominates, original is struck through, discount percentage is badged prominently. The strategic challenge was balancing four SKUs per graphic without creating visual noise, requiring tight spatial logic and consistent type sizing across all tiles in a weekly production cycle.

Results & Learnings

Working on weekly promotional cycles under real commercial deadlines taught me that design decisions have direct business consequences - a wrong price or unclear badge costs customer trust and affects margin. I built a personal QA process to verify price accuracy, spelling, and discount math before every submission. This role gave me direct experience working inside a structured brand system with genuine stakes, sharpening the discipline of professional-grade accuracy.

06 - Personal Practice
Coffee Shop Product Photography
Lifestyle & Product Photography  ·  No Equipment, Just an Eye
+
Target Audience
Cafe Instagram followers 18-30 - atmosphere-seekers, drink inspiration, aesthetic content
Platform
Instagram - Feed Posts
Goal
Communicate the sensory experience of a cafe space without artificial staging
Strategic Rationale

Good product photography for food and beverage is fundamentally about suggesting an experience, not documenting an object. I approached each shot by identifying the emotional quality first: coziness and productivity for the marble table setup with the autumn styling; mystery and richness for the moody copper-tray close-up; quiet, intellectual calm for the bookshelf composition. Natural light and the venue's own atmosphere did the heavy lifting. My job was composition, angle, and patience. The goal in each case was an image that feels discovered, not constructed.

Results & Learnings

These shots were personal practice - no brief, no client. Which is exactly the point. They demonstrate the ability to walk into a space with just a phone and produce images that look intentional, brand-appropriate, and platform-ready. The three different moods from the same environment also demonstrate visual range: the ability to shift tone based on what a brand needs, not just what is easiest to capture.

Final Reflection
Looking Back.
Moving Forward.
"I am the one who will push back on a campaign idea if the numbers do not support it - and fight for a creative direction if I know it is right for the audience. I do not think those two things are in tension."

Every piece in this portfolio - whether it is a food waste campaign for a dining hall, a weekly sale flyer for a grocery chain, a video that made students actually stop scrolling, or a quiet photo of an iced coffee on a bookshelf - comes from the same instinct: understand the audience first, then build something they actually want to look at.

What I am most proud of is the Fozzy work. Not because it is the most visually exciting - it is not - but because it was the first time I had to make design decisions with real commercial stakes. A wrong price, a blurry image, an unclear discount badge: any of those things costs the brand trust. Learning to work carefully inside a structured system, under time pressure, and get it right every week taught me something no class has: the discipline of professional-grade accuracy.

And the coffee shop photos, because no one asked me to take them. I just saw something worth shooting and went after it. That instinct is the part of me I want employers to know exists too.

This portfolio demonstrates that I can do both: make things that stop people mid-scroll, and explain exactly why those things worked.
